title: Business Central is transitioning to .NET 10
summary: Business Central is transitioning from .NET 8 to .NET 10 across online and on-premises deployments. For online, Microsoft handles the migration automatically during maintenance windows. For on-premises, .NET 10 arrives through cumulative updates (BC 27 at CU 27.12, BC 28 at CU 28.6, BC 29 from release), with corresponding AL Language extension version requirements.
key_points: Online environments migrate to .NET 10 automatically during configured maintenance windows with no manual action needed
On-premises .NET 10 availability depends on cumulative update level, not major version, requiring verification before applying specific CUs
AL Language extension requires .NET 10 and now uses .NET Install Tool for VS Code to automatically download and install the runtime
Cloud-only extensions with pure AL code have no exposure to compatibility issues; on-premises solutions with DotNet interop need assembly compatibility verification
features: .NET Install Tool for Visual Studio Code

quotes.text: For on-prem, .NET 10 arrives through cumulative updates to supported releases.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies that on-premises upgrade timing depends on CU level, not major version, which is critical for deployment planning

quotes.text: If you are cloud only and your extensions are pure AL, you have no exposure.
quotes.why_it_matters: Identifies that most AppSource and cloud solutions are unaffected, reducing scope of migration concerns
